title: Araca
summary: Araca is a south-shore West Neck placename in present-day Amityville, Babylon. It is recorded in a 1697 deed and interpreted as beyond, furthermost, or further, describing its position as the westernmost neck of the old Huntington bounds.
map_geometry_source: Approximate point on the West Neck/Amityville peninsula along Great South Bay; not an exact deed boundary.
why_this_matters: Araca preserves a Native directional name from a 1697 deed for the West Neck area of present-day Amityville, with meanings such as beyond or furthermost. That kind of placename shows how people described land in relation to movement, shorelines, and neighboring places rather than only by fixed modern boundaries. The South Shore is a layered geography where colonial deed language still carries traces of Indigenous spatial knowledge.
introduction_content: Araca, also printed as Arace, is identified with West Neck in Amityville, Babylon town. The name belongs to the south-shore West Neck, not the different West Neck on the north shore near Lloyd Harbor.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include araca and Arace. The word is interpreted as beyond, furthermost, or further. The meaning fits the deed description of the neck as the westernmost neck in the old Huntington bounds.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names may reflect or give rise to feelings of individual and collective identity attached to the places in question.”

— Botolv Helleland, Place Names and Identities (2012), Introduction
whereintheworld_content: Araca preserves how Native place names described position, water boundaries, and relationships between neighboring necks of land. It also helps keep the south-shore Amityville West Neck distinct from other Long Island places with similar English names.
